title: Fix embedded skill UI app asset path normalization
description: Arrow.js mini-app skills using ui-app entry values like 'assets/index.html' do not render in the web UI because the iframe/open-tab URL builder also prefixes /assets/, yielding /assets/assets/index.html. Normalize ui-app entry handling and add regression coverage for the documented assets/index.html form.

title: Build benchmark-driven harness improvement loop and deterministic skill verification
description:
Investigate and implement the parts of the autoagent methodology that fit homeclaw.

Context
- The useful part of autoagent is not its runtime harness. It is the benchmark-driven improvement loop: establish a baseline, change prompt/tools/orchestration, rerun evals, keep only improvements, and log every experiment.
- homeclaw already has a stronger runtime harness for household use: prompt and response rules, privacy enforcement, tool routing, skill creation/install/update, and background consolidation.
- The main gap is a lack of a scored, repeatable harness evaluation loop for real homeclaw behaviors.

Why this matters
- We need a disciplined way to improve response quality, tool use, skill creation, and determinism over time.
- Prompt growth alone is a weak improvement strategy. We need evidence-based changes backed by evals and tighter verification.
- The current system has several high-variance areas that should be made more deterministic, especially skill activation, skill verification, and tool-use validation.

Goals
- Build a repeatable eval loop for homeclaw behavior and harness changes.
- Make improvements measurable with baseline, rerun, and keep/discard criteria.
- Improve deterministic behavior around tool selection, side effects, privacy boundaries, and final responses.
- Add verification for generated or installed skills before treating them as production-ready.

Non-goals
- Do not import autoagent's single-file coding harness or coding-task assumptions.
- Do not run autonomous self-editing against production household data.
- Do not optimize for generic coding benchmarks; optimize for household assistant behavior.

Workstreams
1. Behavior eval corpus
- Create a deterministic eval suite for real homeclaw tasks using fixed household fixtures.
- Cover reply quality, tool selection, file side effects, privacy enforcement, memory writes, reminders, bookmarks, and routine behavior.
- Prefer deterministic assertions for correctness; use LLM-as-judge only for narrow style/tone checks.

2. Harness experiment loop
- Add a harness experiment runner that records baseline and variant results.
- Keep changes only when behavior improves, or stays equal while the implementation becomes simpler.
- Record experiment metadata and per-case outcomes for regression analysis.

3. Skill verification and certification
- Add a verification path for skill_create, skill_install, and skill_update.
- Verify parsing, loading, dependency availability, namespaced tool registration, sample scenarios, and data-file conventions.
- Distinguish between a skill that exists on disk and a skill that is verified for use.

4. Deterministic runtime improvements
- Reduce prompt-only behavior where repeated failures can be handled with explicit tools or validators.
- Replace LLM-generated activity-feed summaries with deterministic templates where possible.
- Make skill activation session-scoped instead of process-global.
- Tighten tool classification and routing based on eval evidence rather than intuition.

5. Response-quality controls
- Define measurable standards for concise replies, useful interim updates, and completion behavior after tool calls.
- Add regression cases for common bad patterns: empty acknowledgements, overlong responses, promising actions without tools, and weak follow-through after writes.

Acceptance criteria
- There is a committed eval corpus for core household assistant behaviors.
- There is a documented baseline/variant/keep-discard workflow for harness changes.
- Skill verification exists and is applied to create/install/update flows.
- At least one current nondeterministic runtime behavior is replaced with a deterministic implementation.
- Harness changes can be evaluated with a repeatable score or pass/fail report instead of ad hoc judgment.

Suggested child issues
- Build eval fixtures and scoring harness for core homeclaw behaviors.
- Add skill_verify and wire it into skill creation/install/update flows.
- Make skill activation session-scoped and deterministic.
- Replace LLM tool-feed summaries with deterministic summaries.
- Define and test response-style regression cases.
- Document the harness improvement workflow for contributors.

References
- autoagent repo: https://github.com/kevinrgu/autoagent/tree/main
- autoagent directive/program: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kevinrgu/autoagent/main/program.md

title: Support Arrow.js embedded mini-apps in skills
description: Skills can store files in data/ and assets/ directories, and the agent can read/write them, but the web UI has no way to render a skill's HTML as an embedded app. This issue tracks adding that capability using Arrow.js as the target framework. ## Context Arrow.js (https://arrow-js.com) is a zero-build reactive micro-library (~5KB). A skill can write a single index.html using Arrow.js with no compilation step, making it viable for agent-generated UIs. The skill can store state in data/ as JSON and read it via the existing /api/skills/{owner}/{name}/files/ endpoints. ## What exists today - Skills can declare an assets/ directory alongside data/, scripts/, references/ - GET /api/skills/{owner}/{name}/files/{path} reads any file from the skill root, but returns it as an API response — not served as a document - The web UI (ui/src/views/Skills.svelte) is a file browser + editor only — no preview or embedded panel - homeclaw-planning-prompt.md references a has_ui_panel metadata field but it is not implemented anywhere There is no way to serve skill HTML as a page or embed it in the UI today. ## What needs to be built ### 1. Asset-serving endpoint (backend) Add GET /api/skills/{owner}/{name}/assets/{file_path} to homeclaw/api/routes/skills.py. - Serve files from skill_dir/assets/ with correct MIME types (.html, .js, .css, .json, etc.) - Path traversal guard (same as existing _safe_path() pattern) - No auth required for GET (assets are served inline in the UI, which is already authed) - Scope: household skills accessible to any authed user; personal skills to that member only ### 2. SKILL.md frontmatter declaration Extend the skill frontmatter schema in homeclaw/plugins/skills/loader.py to support: ui-app: entry: assets/index.html # default title: "My App" # optional display name When present, skills are flagged as having a UI app. This flag surfaces in GET /api/skills/{owner}/{name} so the frontend knows to render a panel. ### 3. UI panel (frontend) In ui/src/views/Skills.svelte (or a new SkillApp.svelte component), add a panel that: - Checks if skill has ui_app in its metadata - Renders an iframe pointing to /api/skills/{owner}/{name}/assets/index.html - Uses sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" so the app can call back to /api/ for data - Provides a fallback link to open in new tab ### 4. Update skill-creator instructions Add to homeclaw/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md the Arrow.js mini-app pattern showing: - assets/index.html with Arrow.js loaded from CDN - how to fetch skill data from /api/skills/{owner}/{name}/files/data/state.json - SKILL.md frontmatter declaring ui-app ## Example Arrow.js skill app assets/index.html: ## Gaps and risks - Arrow.js imports from CDN — LAN-only installs would need CDN reachable or library vendored into assets/. Safe default: vendor a copy in the reference skill. - iframe sandbox attribute: allow-same-origin lets the app call /api/ but also allows localStorage access — this is the right tradeoff for same-origin embedded apps - The asset-serving endpoint must not expose files outside the skill's assets/ directory (path traversal guard required) - The agent needs to know to generate Arrow.js apps when creating UI skills; update skill-creator SKILL.md to document the pattern ## Key files - homeclaw/api/routes/skills.py — add asset-serving endpoint - homeclaw/plugins/skills/loader.py (lines 28-146) — extend frontmatter schema, expose ui_app flag in SkillDefinition - ui/src/views/Skills.svelte — add conditional iframe panel - homeclaw/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md — document the Arrow.js pattern for the agent - homeclaw/api/app.py (lines 73-83) — reference for static file mounting
close_reason: Implemented. PR #121. ui-app: frontmatter, /assets/ serving endpoint, query-param auth, iframe panel in Skills.svelte, Arrow.js pattern in skill-creator SKILL.md.

title: Handle stringified allowed_domains in skill frontmatter
description: Embedded app skill creation can leave allowed_domains as the YAML string "[]" in SKILL.md. read_skill then crashes in parse_skill_md/SkillFrontmatter because the loader only accepts a native list. Harden frontmatter parsing to normalize stringified empty and JSON-style arrays, and add regression coverage for read_skill/loader behavior.
close_reason: Fixed loader to normalize stringified allowed_domains and added regression tests

title: Make embedded skill UI creation deterministic
description: Harden skill UI creation/repair flows so public users do not get stuck. Add deterministic guards that reject data_write to SKILL.md/assets, validate and normalize ui-app frontmatter, provide a dedicated helper to enable/create embedded ui-app files, and add regression tests for existing-skill repair flows.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic embedded skill UI flow with dedicated helper, validation, and regression coverage

title: Split overloaded built-in tools into single-purpose variants
description: Reduce model confusion by introducing single-purpose replacements for overloaded built-in tools. Start with skill file operations (read/write/replace), memory topic reads vs listing, and contact create vs update. Preserve compatibility but update prompt/guidance/tests to prefer the explicit variants.
close_reason: Added single-purpose tool variants for file, memory, and contact flows

title: Document conventional PR titles for release-please
